Creston Industrial · 2027 medical strategy

Stay on the marketplace stipend, or offer a group plan?

What 2027 costs look like for Creston and for your people, and our recommendation.

Wednesday, November 11, 2026 · Kim Hildebrand, Christina Heyboer, Paul
Presented by Jason Bearup · Draft for discussion

Today

Where Creston is today

  • No group medical since 2025. Employees buy their own marketplace plan.
  • Creston pays a stipend every paycheck: the part of the employee's net premium above a cap. It is taxable pay.
  • Caps: $300/mo single, $700/mo family. Couples: $375 or $700, to confirm.
  • Opt-out: $30 per paycheck in the Dec 2025 worksheet ($60 elsewhere; to confirm).
  • About 13 households on the marketplace with a paid 2026 plan.

Considerations

Things to weigh

Subsidies end with an affordable offer

If the employee's share of single coverage is no more than 10.22% of household income (2027), the family loses marketplace subsidies. 4 households have one today.

Taxes favor group

The stipend is taxable pay (Creston FICA 7.65%, plus employee FICA and income tax). Group contributions and payroll deductions are pre-tax.

Carrier minimums

Group plans have participation and employer contribution minimums. To confirm with Priority Health.

More people may enroll

Employees taking the opt-out today may join a group plan, which raises the total cost.

Network

Corewell Health West Michigan is what most employees use today. Which providers are Tier 1 in West MI Partners: to confirm with PH.

Benchmark problem goes away

On group there is no benchmark to pick by county; everyone gets the same base plan and the same rule.

Recommendation

Our recommendation: a Priority Health base plan with buy-ups

Base plan: PH PriorityHSA HMO Bronze B85

  • The lowest-cost Priority Health plan we priced: ~$8,715/mo for the 10 rated households vs ~$9,375 for S40. Matching today's caps, it costs Creston ~$42.5K/yr vs ~$50K for S40 on that basis.
  • Creston pays a flat $491 per employee per month toward the base plan: ~$68K/yr for 12 enrollees, inside the ~$64K–$71K budget.
  • Employees who want a lower deductible buy up and pay the difference, pre-tax.
  • One plan family, one rule, no benchmark to pick, no payroll tax on Creston's share.

Trade-off: the 4 subsidized households lose their subsidy, and some pay more. Most others pay the same or less than today.

Next steps

Next steps to a 1/1/2027 group plan

  1. Set Creston's contribution

    Pick the fixed amount toward the HSA B85 base plan, within ~$64K–$71K/yr.

  2. Confirm the census and eligibility

    Who is employed and eligible, and which opt-outs would join. More enrollees spread the budget thinner.

  3. Final Priority Health quote

    Base plan plus the S40, S25, S35 and HMO B85 buy-ups for everyone enrolling (2 households not yet rated), with tobacco status. Confirm participation and contribution minimums.

  4. Network check and decision date

    Confirm West MI Partners Tier 1 providers with PH. Set a decision date that makes 1/1/2027 (carrier deadline to confirm); marketplace open enrollment ends 1/15/2027.
